task_spec.title: Executive brief
task_spec.objective: Write a one-page brief (no more than 600 words) for the head of claims summarising what this piece of work found, using only the saved results of the earlier tasks in this run: the description of the book, the denial analysis, the provider and network comparison and the high-cost model. Cover the key findings, how the model performed, the limitations and what to do next. Produce the standard artifacts (executive brief, findings table, report).

component_catalogue.description: Extract headline metrics from the final attempt of chosen source tasks under the same run and condition; missing sources are recorded, never invented.

sources.description: Which earlier tasks' saved metrics feed the brief.

produces.shape: [{task_id: str, metric_key: str, label: str, value, numerator?: int, denominator?: int, source_path: str}] or {task_id, status: missing}

component_catalogue.description: Compose executive_brief.md from the collected findings with chosen sections, language style and citation policy.

causal_language.description: Whether the brief may phrase relationships causally ("X drives Y") or only associatively ("X is associated with Y").

cite_artifacts.description: Whether every numeric statement ends with a [source: <path>] citation.

produces.shape: {sections: [str], causal_language: str, cite_artifacts: bool, word_count: int, n_numeric_statements: int, n_cited_statements: int}

component_catalogue.description: Write report.md with summary, results, artifacts, caveats and method sections.

caveats.description: Which fixed caveat statements to include in the report's Caveats section.

show_denominators.description: Whether every rate in the report is printed as numerator / denominator = rate.

cite_artifacts.description: Whether every results bullet ends with a [source: ...] reference to an artifact or metrics key.

plan.rationale: This revised plan addresses all three feedback items from the prior evaluation. First, it expands collect_findings sources from [T2, T6] to [T2, T5, T6, T7] to include all major analytical outputs—denial analysis (T2), fraud exploration (T5), and both predictive models (T6, T7)—improving completeness and providing comprehensive context for executive decision-making. Second, it enables cite_artifacts in brief_sections to ensure every numeric statement carries a [source: ...] citation, directly addressing the reproducibility gap where 0 of 5 numeric statements were previously cited. The brief structure remains focused on key findings, model results, limitations, and next steps, with causal language avoided to prevent misinterpretation of descriptive and comparative results. The write_report component maintains all four critical caveats (synthetic_data, descriptive_only, association_not_causation, no_operational_use) through applied skills, protecting readers from misinterpreting findings or deploying analytical results operationally without proper validation.
plan.changes_summary: Expanded collect_findings sources from [T2, T6] to [T2, T5, T6, T7] to include fraud exploration and second model; enabled cite_artifacts in brief_sections to ensure all numeric statements are cited to their source artifacts, addressing reproducibility gap.

feedback.remediation: Collect findings from the portfolio (T2), fraud exploration (T5) and both models (T6, T7).
Cite the source artifact or metrics key after every numeric statement (brief_sections cite_artifacts true).
Every numeric statement in the brief must carry a [source: ...] citation (n_cited_statements must equal n_numeric_statements).
Include at least one of the provider (T3) or denial (T4) analyses among the sources.
Include key findings, model results, limitations, synthetic-data caveats and next steps as sections of the brief.

reusable_lessons.lesson: When synthesizing analyses into an executive brief, collect findings from all major analytical workstreams (denial analysis, fraud exploration, predictive models, and segmentation analyses) to ensure decision-makers receive comprehensive context for strategic decisions.

Establish citation discipline as a standard practice in executive communication: every numeric statement must carry a source citation to the artifact or metrics key from which it derives. This ensures reproducibility and protects credibility across all executive-level deliverables.

Executive briefs that synthesize portfolio analyses must incorporate findings from segmentation workstreams (provider network status, denial reason distributions, claim type patterns) to contextualize aggregate metrics and ground recommendations in claim-level evidence.

When presenting analyses of synthetic or simulated data in executive communication, include a dedicated 'synthetic_caveats' or 'data_provenance' section as a required structural element. This explicit disclosure protects against misapplication of findings in operational decisions where clinical validation and governance review are required.

current_task_corrections.correction: Add T3 (provider network comparison) or T4 (denial analysis segmentation) to the collect_findings sources parameter to provide segmentation context that illuminates claim and provider patterns in the executive brief.

Add 'synthetic_caveats' to the brief_sections sections parameter to include a dedicated section disclosing the synthetic nature of the data and its implications for applying the findings operationally.

existing_skills.name: document_synthetic_data_limitations_in_all_reports
existing_skills.objective: Ensure all reports clearly disclose that the data is synthetic and that observed patterns, distributions, and anomalies may not reflect real-world claims characteristics.
procedure: When writing the report for any task involving synthetic or simulated claims data, include the 'synthetic_data' caveat in the report's Caveats section.

Phrase the caveat to clearly state that the dataset is synthetic or simulated, and explicitly note that findings, patterns, and numerical results should not be interpreted as representative of actual claims behavior.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section so readers encounter it before interpreting any results.
required_checks: Verify that the report includes the synthetic_data caveat either as a listed caveat item or as explicit phrasing in the report text.
Check that the caveat language clearly identifies the data as synthetic and disclaims generalizability to real-world claims.

existing_skills.name: include_descriptive_analysis_caveat_in_all_reports
existing_skills.objective: Ensure all descriptive analysis reports include a caveat explicitly stating that the analysis is descriptive only and supports no causal or operational conclusions, protecting readers from misinterpretation of findings
procedure: When using the write_report component for any descriptive claims analysis, include the 'descriptive_only' caveat in the report component's caveats parameter.

Phrase the caveat to clearly state that the analysis is descriptive in nature and that findings, distributions, and patterns should not be interpreted as supporting causal claims or operational decisions without further investigation.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section so readers encounter the limitation before interpreting results.
required_checks: Verify that 'descriptive_only' is listed among the report component's caveats or that equivalent descriptive-analysis disclaimer language is present in the report text.
Confirm that the caveat language clearly identifies the analysis as descriptive and disclaims causal and operational interpretation.

existing_skills.name: use_adjudicated_claims_as_denominator_for_segment_rates
existing_skills.objective: Establish the correct statistical denominator (adjudicated claims) when calculating segment-level rates, enabling valid comparisons and sound operational decision-making
procedure: When calculating denial rates (or other rates) by segment values (claim_type, provider_specialty, network_status, place_of_service, auth_required_flag, etc.), use only adjudicated claims as the denominator
Define adjudicated claims as those with claim status in {Paid, Denied, Adjusted}, explicitly excluding unadjudicated or pending statuses
Set the denominator_option field to 'adjudicated_claims' and record this choice in all output
Calculate the rate as numerator / adjudicated_claims_denominator for each segment value
Document that this approach provides the correct basis for segment-level rate comparison and operational decision-making
required_checks: Verify denominator_option is set to 'adjudicated_claims' in the output
Confirm each segment's numerator and denominator are aligned within the adjudicated_claims population
Check that segment denominators sum to the total adjudicated claims

existing_skills.name: clarify_associations_not_causation_in_comparative_analysis
existing_skills.objective: Prevent misinterpretation of observed group differences as causal effects by explicitly documenting that findings represent statistical associations, not causal relationships.
procedure: When your analysis reveals differences in metrics (rates, averages, or distributions) across groups or segments, add the 'association_not_causation' caveat to the report's Caveats section.
In the caveat, explicitly state that observed differences represent statistical associations and do not imply causal mechanisms or causal relationships.
Explain that the descriptive analysis cannot determine whether differences arise from causal effects, confounding variables, or other factors outside the scope of the data.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section, before results are presented, so readers understand this interpretive limit.
required_checks: Verify that the report includes the 'association_not_causation' caveat either as a listed caveat item or as explicit language in the report text.
Confirm that the caveat language clearly distinguishes between observed statistical associations and causal relationships.

existing_skills.name: include_no_operational_use_caveat_in_healthcare_predictive_m
existing_skills.objective: Prevent operational deployment of analytical models without proper clinical validation, governance review, and risk assessment by explicitly documenting that model scores are analytical tools and must not be used operationally without additional vetting.
procedure: When using the write_report component for any predictive or classification task on healthcare or claims data, assess whether the model output is analytical-only or intended for operational decision-making.
If the model is analytical-only (scoring for review, not automatic decisions), include the 'no_operational_use' caveat in the report component's caveats parameter.

Phrase the caveat to clearly state that the model output is analytical in nature and that scores require clinical validation, governance review, and organizational risk assessment before any operational use, such as automated coverage decisions or claim payment instructions.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section so readers understand this critical limitation before interpreting or acting on results.
required_checks: Verify that 'no_operational_use' is listed among the report component's caveats or that equivalent language about analytical-only status and requirement for validation before operational use is present in the report text.
Confirm that the caveat language explicitly distinguishes between analytical use (for review or investigation) and operational use (for automated decisions or process changes).
Check that the caveat mentions validation and governance review as prerequisites for operational deployment.
